item.title: Night Plane review – join the jumbo jet to hell in this indie horror head trip
item.description: Liquid Static Studio; PC You take on the role of flight attendant in this clever and absorbing retro-style game that veers from daft horror spoof to genuinely disturbing There was always something creepy about the job-simulator genre. All those mindless automatons queueing up to use your bus, bar or bed store, or whatever workplace you are trapped in for the duration of the game. The endless repetitive tasks. The emptiness of the world beyond your corporate existence. Together, these elements scream existential terror … which is perhaps why we are now seeing a new indie sub-genre of job sim… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.

item.title: 2,000-year-old Roman bread found inside oven after Mount Vesuvius volcanic eruption
item.description: A loaf of bread left inside an oven in Herculaneum during the AD 79 eruption of Mount Vesuvius was discovered carbonised during excavations in 1930. The nearly 2,000-year-old find offers a glimpse into ancient Roman food habits. The British Museum later recreated the bread, while other preserved loaves reveal how Romans divided bread into portions and used stamps to identify it. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Metropolis: more than four decades of street photography – in pictures
item.description: Metropolis: Street Photography 1985–2025 transitions from the tough, film-noir streets of 1980s New York, to the time surrounding the fall of the Berlin Wall, to the modern, colour-saturated, hard-shadowed geometry of contemporary Australian streets. Spanning classic monochrome grit and vivid colour abstraction, this remarkable collection examines how photographers have documented the relentless energy of our ever-changing cities. Ultimately, it is a celebration of the unscripted characters, strange encounters and the absurd comedy that unfolds when people share public space. On now until 17… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.
item.dc:creator: Guardian Staff

item.title: Hay un motivo por el que los combates de 'Phantom Blade: Zero' parecen una película de artes marciales: Jackie Chan
item.description: Cuando vimos por primera vez 'Phantom Blade: Zero' en el PlayStation Showcase de mayo de 2023 , muchos pensaron que aquellos combates tan rápidos y espectaculares parecían secuencias de una película de acción. No era casualidad. El proyecto del estudio chino S-GAME lleva años desarrollándose con una idea muy concreta: trasladar al videojuego la precisión, las acrobacias y la contundencia del cine de artes marciales y qué mejor referencia que el propio Jackie Chan. El resultado ha convencido a la crítica y está a punto de llegar al mercado: se estrena el 29 de octubre para PC y PlayStation 5… Fuente: Xataka.
